evals.name: autonomous-dispatches-even-when-plan-is-all-main-window
evals.prompt: /implementation:implement-dispatch — execute the approved plan. This is an autonomous goal-loop run with no human in the turn cycle; the plan's routing table lists every phase as main-window.
evals.expected_output: Detects autonomous orchestration mode and dispatches scope-fenced workers per phase anyway — orchestrated cadence is the default in autonomous mode even when the plan routes all-main-window, so it synthesizes per-phase worker rows rather than doing volume edits from the orchestrator, capping concurrent dispatch at 3-5 workers.
expectations: Detects autonomous mode from the goal-loop / no-human-in-cycle signal
Dispatches workers per phase even though the routing table is all main-window — synthesizes worker rows rather than editing inline
Does NOT perform the volume edits itself from the orchestrator window in autonomous mode
Caps concurrent dispatch at roughly 3-5 workers per wave

evals.name: interactive-all-main-window-hands-back-to-implement
evals.prompt: /implementation:implement-dispatch — this is an interactive session with me reviewing each turn, and the approved plan has no routing table (all phases are main-window).
evals.expected_output: In interactive mode with no worker rows in the routing table, hands execution back to /implementation:implement's classic inline cadence instead of dispatching workers — dispatch is only for worker-routed phases here.
expectations: Detects interactive mode (human reviewing each turn) rather than autonomous
Hands back to /implementation:implement classic inline cadence because the routing table is absent / all main-window
Does NOT force worker dispatch onto an interactive all-main-window plan

evals.name: verifies-worker-return-against-direct-evidence
evals.prompt: /implementation:implement-dispatch phase-2 — the worker for phase 2 reported back: 'Done, all files updated and the build is green.' Accept the phase and move on.
evals.expected_output: Treats the worker return as synthesis, not ground truth: promotes its claims to direct evidence (diff read, grep, file Read) and runs /toolchain:check itself main-side before accepting the edits — it never accepts the worker's green claim as the build signal.
expectations: Does NOT accept the worker's 'build is green' claim as the authoritative build signal
Verifies the worker's claims against direct evidence (reads the diff / greps / reads files) before building on them
Runs /toolchain:check itself from the main window rather than trusting the worker's report

evals.name: brief-carries-scope-fence-and-divergence-clause
evals.prompt: /implementation:implement-dispatch phase-1 — compose the brief and dispatch the worker for phase 1.
evals.expected_output: The composed brief carries an explicit scope fence (enumerated ALLOWED and FORBIDDEN files/actions), the verbatim divergence-escalation clause instructing the worker to STOP and report if an assumption proves wrong or it must touch anything FORBIDDEN, the touched project invariants, and the phase acceptance criteria — before dispatching.
expectations: The brief enumerates an explicit scope fence: ALLOWED vs FORBIDDEN files/actions
The brief includes the verbatim divergence-escalation clause (STOP and report on a wrong assumption or a FORBIDDEN touch — do not improvise)
The brief includes the phase's acceptance criteria and the project invariants the task touches
The scope fence and clause are present before dispatch, not added after the worker returns

evals.name: non-interactive-moderate-divergence-takes-conservative-option
evals.prompt: /implementation:implement-dispatch — autonomous run, no human to escalate to. A worker hit a moderate divergence: the plan named a config key that turned out slightly different, and it's asking how to proceed.
evals.expected_output: In a non-interactive run, moderate divergence does not deadlock the run: it picks the conservative option (truest to the plan's intent, smallest blast radius), logs it to a DEVIATIONS.md beside the plan artifact, and keeps going. Major divergence would still STOP even autonomously.
expectations: Does NOT deadlock the autonomous run waiting for a human on a moderate divergence
Picks the conservative option (closest to plan intent, smallest blast radius) for the moderate divergence
Logs the deviation to a DEVIATIONS.md beside the plan artifact (what was planned, what was done, why, blast radius)
The logged entry is typed (plan-confirmed / discovery / deviation / human-decision), and a deviation entry answers plan said / found / chose / revisit
Reserves a hard STOP for major divergence (a fundamental assumption wrong), not this moderate one

evals.name: autonomous-fresh-context-verifier-before-done
evals.prompt: /implementation:implement-dispatch — autonomous run. Phase 3 changes behavior (a new validation branch in the order intake path); its workers have returned and their acceptance criteria look met; mark the phase DONE.
evals.expected_output: In autonomous mode, because phase 3 changes behavior, before marking the phase [DONE] it dispatches a fresh-context verifier subagent that checks the phase's acceptance criteria against the actual diff — a separate agent, never the producing context auditing itself — and surfaces that result in the response before ending the turn. It still runs the Step 4 phase-boundary ritual, scaled to residency: plan marks, a DEVIATIONS.md entry, and the commit when it stays resident, and the full ritual when it clears, switches model or domain, or ends the run.
expectations: Dispatches a separate fresh-context verifier subagent before marking the phase DONE (not the producing context self-auditing)
The verifier checks acceptance criteria against the actual diff, and its result is surfaced in the response before the turn ends

At a resident boundary runs plan marks, a DEVIATIONS.md entry, and the commit, keeping the full /implementation:implement Step 4 ritual (handoff, status summary, resume prompt) for a clear, a model or domain switch, or run end
A mechanical, behavior-preserving phase is verified by the orchestrator from the diff plus the build/test signal, with no verifier spawn, in every mode

evals.name: wave-cap-argument-overrides-internal-default
evals.prompt: /implementation:implement-dispatch --wave-cap 2 — autonomous run, execute the approved plan; a phase routes eight parallelizable worker rows with disjoint fences, and the plan declares commit authority orchestrator in one assigned worktree.
evals.expected_output: The passed --wave-cap 2 replaces the internal 3–5 default: a wave is a batch of that phase's worker rows, so at most 2 rows are in flight at once and the eight rows run as sequential waves of at most 2 rather than 3–5. The rows can share the assigned worktree only because the orchestrator is its only git writer; they keep disjoint fences, none stages, and the build/test gate runs after each wave settles. With no --wave-cap the internal 3–5 default would stand instead; the argument is the single enforcement point for a caller-configured concurrency ceiling and does not otherwise change the dispatch cadence. A fractional cap (e.g. --wave-cap 2.5) is floored to whole rows (2), and a value below 1 is treated as 1 — never a fractional or zero cap.
expectations: Honors --wave-cap 2 as the ceiling on worker rows in flight at once within the phase, capping at 2 rather than the internal 3–5
Runs the eight rows as sequential waves of at most 2 within the one phase, never starting a later phase's rows alongside them
Shares the assigned worktree only under the declared orchestrator authority: disjoint fences, no worker stages, and the build/test gate runs after each wave settles
Treats the argument as the only change — the rest of the dispatch cadence (scope-fenced briefs, verify-returns, main-side build) is unchanged
Floors a fractional cap to whole rows and treats a value below 1 as 1 — never a fractional or zero cap

evals.name: no-commit-plan-fence-declares-orchestrator-commit-authority
evals.prompt: /implementation:implement-dispatch phase-1 - the approved plan's worker fence forbids staging, committing, and pushing: the orchestrator owns a commit-subject gate, and the plan pushes once at the end. The phase-1 worktree already exists at C:/work/wt-phase1. Compose the brief and dispatch the worker.
evals.expected_output: Declares commit authority orchestrator explicitly in the brief, dispatches the implementation:implementer agent rather than a generic subagent, omits the commit-and-push-early clause and worker-side provisioning, hands over the assigned worktree path, and verifies the return against the uncommitted tree before the orchestrator commits the phase source at the phase boundary without pushing. A fence that forbade only a narrow action such as force-push would leave commit authority at worker.
expectations: The brief declares commit authority orchestrator explicitly rather than leaving the worker to infer it from the fence

Dispatches the implementation:implementer agent, not a generic subagent type, and the brief omits the commit-and-push-early clause and any worker-side provisioning while giving the assigned worktree path
Verifies the return against the uncommitted tree (status --porcelain including untracked entries, diff HEAD) and runs the build/test gate on it
The orchestrator commits the phase source in one phase-boundary commit under its commit-subject gate and does not push before the plan's single push
Does NOT treat a fence forbidding only a narrow action (for example force-push or opening the PR) as switching commit authority to orchestrator

evals.name: worker-authority-rows-sharing-a-worktree-run-one-at-a-time
evals.prompt: /implementation:implement-dispatch phase-2 --wave-cap 3 — autonomous run; phase 2 routes two independent worker rows with disjoint fences, both editing in the item's one persisted worktree, and no brief declares a commit authority.
evals.expected_output: Commit authority is worker, the default for an absent field, so each row stages, commits, and pushes early in the shared worktree. One git writer per worktree binds under both authorities: the two rows dispatch one at a time (a wave of one in that worktree) even though --wave-cap 3 would allow three, with the second dispatched after the first returns. Running them concurrently would need commit authority orchestrator declared in both briefs, where the orchestrator is the only git writer. The skill does not split the worktree or provision a second one to get parallelism.
expectations: Treats the absent commit-authority field as worker, and does not dispatch the two rows concurrently into the one shared worktree
Explains that --wave-cap 3 does not lift the one-writer-per-worktree rule: under worker, rows sharing a worktree run one per wave
Names commit authority orchestrator, declared in the briefs rather than inferred, as the only way to run both rows at once in that worktree
Does NOT provision a per-row worktree or split the phase's briefs to manufacture parallelism

evals.name: wave-fences-composed-disjoint-before-dispatch
evals.prompt: /implementation:implement-dispatch phase-3 — autonomous run, commit authority orchestrator in one assigned worktree. Phase 3 has three worker rows: row A may edit src/order/*.py, row B may edit src/order/intake.py and src/pricing/*.py, row C may edit tests/order/*.py. Compose the briefs and dispatch the wave.
evals.expected_output: Before dispatching any row, the orchestrator composes the three ALLOWED sets together and finds that rows A and B both allow src/order/intake.py. Overlapping rows do not go out as one wave: it narrows the fences so they are disjoint by file path, or runs the overlapping rows in sequential waves. Each dispatched row's FORBIDDEN list carries the paths the other rows of its wave own, so a touch on a sibling's path trips the divergence-escalation clause. The briefs list paths only, never which row or worker owns them.
expectations: Detects that rows A and B both allow src/order/intake.py before dispatching any row
Does NOT dispatch A and B in the same wave with overlapping ALLOWED sets; narrows the fences to disjoint paths or runs them in sequential waves
Adds each same-wave sibling's owned paths to every row's FORBIDDEN list
Measures disjointness on the file path written, not on which worktree the row writes from
Lists paths in each brief without naming which row or worker owns them

evals.name: operator-wave-cap-applies-when-no-argument
evals.prompt: /implementation:implement-dispatch phase-3 — autonomous run, no human in the turn cycle. Phase 3 has six worker rows with disjoint fences, commit authority orchestrator. No --wave-cap was passed; the operator configured implement_dispatch_wave_cap = 2.
evals.expected_output: Reads the operator's implement_dispatch_wave_cap because no --wave-cap argument was passed, and runs phase 3's six rows as three sequential waves of two rather than applying the internal 3-5 default.
expectations: Uses the operator's implement_dispatch_wave_cap value (2) as the wave cap because no --wave-cap argument was passed
Runs no more than two worker rows at once, so the six rows run as sequential waves
Does NOT apply the internal 3-5 default while the operator option is configured
States that a --wave-cap argument, had one been passed, would take precedence over the operator option

evals.name: post-phase-source-commit-gets-fresh-verifier
evals.prompt: /implementation:implement-dispatch — autonomous run, no human in the turn cycle. Every numbered phase is marked [DONE]. The orchestrator then made one more source edit in the main window, a bug fix to a helper, and is about to push the branch and open the PR.
evals.expected_output: Dispatches implementation:phase-verifier over the post-phase diff with the orchestrator's rationale withheld, spawns no worker, and neither pushes nor opens the PR until the verdict returns; an INCONCLUSIVE verdict is not treated as a pass.
expectations: Dispatches implementation:phase-verifier as a fresh-context pass over the post-phase diff before pushing or opening a PR
Withholds the orchestrator's rationale and reasoning from the verifier's brief
Spawns no worker for the post-phase change
Does NOT push or create the PR before the verifier's verdict returns
Does NOT treat an INCONCLUSIVE verdict as a pass

evals.name: per-phase-model-column-routes-the-worker-agent
evals.prompt: /implementation:implement-dispatch: autonomous run on the Anthropic API (no CLAUDE_CODE_USE_* provider variable is set). The orchestrator's standing rule is to pass model: opus on every spawn. The plan's routing table has Model sonnet on phase 1 (a closed file list with grep checks), no routing row for phase 2, and phase 3 is an auth-token handling change in the security-surface work class. Dispatch each phase in order.
evals.expected_output: Phase 1 dispatches implementation:scoped-implementer with an explicit per-invocation model: sonnet, so the orchestrator's model: opus habit cannot override the routed tier; before that it reads the provider variables with printenv, and would have spawned implementation:implementer instead had a Bedrock, Vertex or Foundry variable been set with ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_SONNET_MODEL unset. Phase 2 has no row, so it dispatches implementation:implementer on its frontmatter binding. Phase 3 is security-surface work, so it dispatches implementation:implementer with the frontier tier's current alias as the per-invocation model. No phase is routed downward by passing a weaker model to implementation:implementer.
expectations: Dispatches phase 1 as implementation:scoped-implementer with an explicit per-invocation model: sonnet, not the orchestrator's model: opus habit

Checks the provider variables (CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK, CLAUDE_CODE_USE_VERTEX, CLAUDE_CODE_USE_FOUNDRY among them) and ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_SONNET_MODEL with printenv before the sonnet dispatch, and names implementation:implementer as the fallback when a provider variable is set and the Sonnet alias override is unset
Dispatches the unrouted phase 2 as implementation:implementer on its frontmatter binding
Dispatches the security-surface phase 3 as implementation:implementer at the frontier tier's current alias
Does NOT pass a model weaker than the binding to implementation:implementer to reach Sonnet

evals.name: heavy-window-signal-routes-not-clears
evals.prompt: /implementation:implement-dispatch: interactive run, phase 3 of 5 in .work/search/PLAN.md was just verified and committed. A context-guard line just reported the window is heavy. Phase 4 is worker-routed, same model.
evals.expected_output: Resident-vs-clear item (a) fires, but it no longer means a default clear: the orchestrator routes the next step with `/session-flow:workflow`, handing it .work/search/PLAN.md and phase 4, and clears to resume from the emitted prompt only if the router routes there. It does not restate the compact/clear/handoff rule itself.
expectations: It routes the boundary through `/session-flow:workflow` with the PLAN.md path and phase 4
It does NOT clear by default just because the heavy-window signal fired
It does NOT state its own rule for when to compact, clear or hand off

evals.name: worker-edits-existing-test-fails-verification
evals.prompt: /implementation:implement-dispatch: autonomous run, phase 2 of .work/rates/PLAN.md adds currency rounding to src/rates/convert.ts. The plan names no test changes for this phase. The worker returned green; its diff changes src/rates/convert.ts and also edits an expected value in the existing test tests/rates/convert.test.ts.
evals.expected_output: Existing test files were FORBIDDEN for this non-test-authoring phase (brief item 1.12), so the return fails verification: the orchestrator does not accept the diff or build on it, reverts or re-briefs the worker, and treats the worker's green claim as no signal. Because the run is unattended, it recommends the testing plugin's `test_guards_enabled` option when it is off.
expectations: It rejects the return because the diff edits an existing test file the phase did not authorize
It reverts or re-briefs rather than accepting the edit to tests/rates/convert.test.ts
It does NOT treat the worker's green report as the build signal
It recommends enabling the testing plugin's `test_guards_enabled` option for the unattended run

evals.name: holdout-tests-stay-off-unless-opted-in
evals.prompt: /implementation:implement-dispatch: autonomous run of .work/auth/PLAN.md, phase 1 of 3. The plan's execution shape says nothing about holdout tests and the user did not ask for them. Compose the phase 1 brief.
evals.expected_output: Holdout acceptance tests are opt-in, so the orchestrator composes the normal brief (fence with existing tests FORBIDDEN, acceptance criteria, reason, commit authority, design excerpt) and writes no holdout tests. It does not turn the option on itself.
expectations: It composes the phase 1 brief without writing holdout tests
It does NOT enable holdout tests on its own initiative
The brief's fence lists existing test files as FORBIDDEN

evals.name: wide-wave-pilots-one-row-first
evals.prompt: /implementation:implement-dispatch phase-2 --wave-cap 5 — autonomous run, commit authority orchestrator in one assigned worktree. Phase 2 has five worker rows with disjoint fences. You dispatch the first row and it returns with a usage-limit error.
evals.expected_output: Because the wave is wider than about 4 rows, the orchestrator dispatches one row alone first rather than all five at once, waits for its return, and checks that plan usage remains before sending the other four. The pilot returned a usage-limit error, so it withholds the remaining four rows and reports the limit instead of dispatching them.
expectations: Dispatches exactly one row first, not all five at once
Waits for the pilot's return and checks remaining plan usage before dispatching the other rows
Withholds the remaining four rows after the pilot returns a usage-limit error and reports it

evals.name: worktree-brief-runs-cwd-sensitive-command-by-directory-flag
evals.prompt: /implementation:implement-dispatch phase-1 — the worker edits in the dedicated worktree /srv/worktrees/app-phase1, outside the session's working directories. The phase's acceptance check is the repository's Makefile `test` target and its `npm run lint` script, both of which read their configuration from the working directory. Compose the brief.
evals.expected_output: The brief gives the worktree's absolute path written literally and anchors every command on it: `git -C <path>` for git, absolute paths elsewhere, one plain command per call, and no `cd`, including a `cd` into the worktree itself. The working-directory-sensitive commands run through their own directory flags, `make -C /srv/worktrees/app-phase1 test` and `npm --prefix /srv/worktrees/app-phase1 run lint`, never as `cd /srv/worktrees/app-phase1 && make test`.
expectations: Writes the worktree path /srv/worktrees/app-phase1 literally in the brief
Directs the Makefile target through `make -C` with the literal worktree path
Directs the lint script through `npm --prefix` with the literal worktree path
Does NOT tell the worker to run any command as `cd <worktree> && <command>`, and states that `cd` is banned even into the worktree

evals.name: worktree-command-without-directory-flag-goes-to-main-side-gate
evals.prompt: /implementation:implement-dispatch phase-2 — the worker edits in the dedicated worktree /srv/worktrees/svc-phase2, outside the session's working directories. The phase's only check is `./check`, a repository wrapper that reads its configuration from the current working directory, takes no directory flag, and does not locate the repository from its own path. Compose the brief and say who runs the check.
evals.expected_output: Because the wrapper has neither a directory flag nor a self-locating path, the brief does not have the worker run it, and in particular never as `cd /srv/worktrees/svc-phase2 && ./check`. The check is left to the orchestrator's main-side gate, which runs it after the worker returns. The brief still anchors the worker's own commands on the literal worktree path with `git -C` and absolute paths and bans `cd`.
expectations: Does NOT instruct the worker to run `./check` via `cd <worktree> && ./check` or any other `cd`
Assigns running `./check` to the orchestrator's main-side gate after the worker returns
Anchors the worker's commands on the literal path /srv/worktrees/svc-phase2 with `git -C` and absolute paths

evals.name: item-list-runs-without-plan-and-holds-unlanded-dependent
evals.prompt: /implementation:implement-dispatch --items .work/ci-perf/findings.md — no PLAN.md exists; the findings file lists F1 (targets scripts/ci/select.sh, acceptance: `bash tests/select.test.sh` passes), F2 (targets scripts/ci/matrix.sh, blocked-by: F1, acceptance: `bash tests/matrix.test.sh` passes) and F3 (targets docs/ci.md, acceptance: markdownlint clean). None is a tracker item. I wrote this list in the item-list shape and approve it. Plan the first wave.
evals.expected_output: Runs the list without asking for a plan. F1 and F3 are ready and go out together with disjoint fences; F2 is held because its declared blocker F1 has not landed on the base, and the run returns F2 as held with that reason rather than dispatching it on F1's unmerged branch. Each dispatched item gets its own fresh-context verifier with its acceptance check as the criteria.
expectations: Does NOT ask for or require a PLAN.md before dispatching
Dispatches F1 and F3 in the first wave with mutually disjoint fences
Holds F2 and names F1 not yet landed on the base as the reason
Gives each dispatched item a phase-verifier whose criteria are that item's acceptance check

evals.name: base-ref-replaces-default-branch-in-worktree-check
evals.prompt: /implementation:implement-dispatch --items items.md --base origin/integration/search — compose the brief for the first item; the worker provisions its own worktree on branch feat/12-index.
evals.expected_output: The brief has the worker cut feat/12-index from origin/integration/search, confirm before its first edit that `git merge-base HEAD origin/integration/search` equals origin/integration/search, STOP on a mismatch, and bring the branch current with origin/integration/search (not the default branch) before returning.
expectations: The base check before the first edit compares against origin/integration/search, written literally
Does NOT check the base against the default branch
Tells the worker to STOP and report on a base mismatch
Brings the branch current with origin/integration/search before returning
